rounds.t: Neural development, neural tube defects, and brain malformations

q.s: Which structure induces the overlying ectoderm to form the neural plate?
e: Correct. It later becomes the nucleus pulposus.
Wrong. Arises from the neural folds.

q.s: The notochord persists in adults as:
The alar plate of the neural tube is induced by which signals and gives rise to which neurons?
The basal (ventral) plate is induced by which signal?
e: Correct. Gives rise to motor neurons.

q.s: Mutations in HOX genes cause which anomalies?
e: Correct. HOX genes regulate segmentation and cranial-caudal differentiation.

q.s: Which vesicle gives rise to the cerebral hemispheres and lateral ventricles?
The retina, thalamus and hypothalamus derive from which vesicle?
The pons and cerebellum develop from the:
e: Correct. With the upper fourth ventricle.

q.s: The cerebral aqueduct is the cavity of which vesicle?
Which cells are derived from neural crest?
o: Schwann cells, dorsal root ganglia and adrenal medulla
e: Correct. Also autonomic ganglia and satellite cells.

q.s: By which week should the neural tube close?
Which maternal finding increases the risk of open neural tube defects?
Which prenatal laboratory findings suggest an open neural tube defect?
o: Elevated maternal serum AFP and amniotic fluid acetylcholinesterase

rounds.t: Holoprosencephaly, lissencephaly, and posterior fossa malformations

q.s: Holoprosencephaly results from:
o: Failure of the forebrain to divide into two cerebral hemispheres

q.s: Holoprosencephaly is associated with which conditions?
o: Patau syndrome and fetal alcohol syndrome

q.s: Patients with holoprosencephaly have an increased risk of which endocrine problem?
o: Pituitary dysfunction such as diabetes insipidus

q.s: Advanced syringomyelia can cause which skeletal and joint findings?
